description:
Residual R-1 from the AS-34 QA review (qa-ruben, --role review comment, 2026-09-02; verdict was PASS 7/7 and this did not block the merge). AS-34 merged at 0b195e5.

WHAT. AS-34 closed symlink-based aliasing on /api/file by requiring the realpath-resolved path to equal the requested path. Hard links are outside that policy: realpathSync does not dereference a hard link, so a file hard-linked to a dot-directory target — the reviewer demonstrated `hardlink.md` hard-linked to `.lattice/plans/task_TEST.md` — serves 200 both on master before AS-34 and on the branch after it. The mechanism AS-34 closed is real and closed; this is a second, different mechanism that was never in scope.

WHY IT IS LOW SEVERITY, AND WHY IT IS NOT ZERO. Creating a hard link needs local write access to the checkout, and anyone with that can simply copy the file to an already-servable path — the same argument that made the original symlink finding low severity. Git cannot represent hard links, so one can never arrive via clone, pull, or checkout. No live exposure exists today: the reviewer's symlink census also found nothing anomalous in the working tree. It is not zero because /api/file is the sole read boundary for a network-reachable container that mounts the whole repo read-only, and because apps/chat/README.md now claims the boundary holds "regardless of how the tree is aliased" — which over-claims by exactly this one mechanism. A documented guarantee that is false in one named case is worse than a narrower true one.

TWO WAYS TO CLOSE IT, DECIDE IN PLANNING:
(a) Narrow the documentation to the mechanism actually covered — cheapest, honest, leaves the gap open by design and says so. Note when writing it that `.claude/` also contains .md files, so the set of dot-directory content reachable by a hard link is not limited to `.lattice/`.
(b) Close the mechanism as well: compare st_dev/st_ino, or reject any served file whose link count exceeds 1, or resolve containment by inode rather than by path. Each has a cost — the link-count test rejects legitimate multi-linked files, and inode comparison changes what "containment" means. Pick one and say why the others were rejected.
Either way the README sentence and the code must agree at the end; today they do not.

ALSO IN SCOPE (residual R-2 from the same review, prose only): apps/chat/README.md lines ~108-110 still summarise the /api/file gate as five checks and omit 3b, the check AS-34 added. Not false in context — the following paragraph describes it — but the enumeration is stale. The reviewer deliberately left it rather than widen AS-34's declared diff.

ACCEPTANCE. If (b) is chosen, a test that plants a hard link in a scratch root and asserts 404, shown red against the unfixed code first (house technique: assert the mutation applied, record the exact failing set, restore under a trap, prove the tree clean). If (a) is chosen, acceptance is prose-only: the README states exactly what is closed and what is not, with no test. Either way: apps/chat suite stays green, no new dependencies, scratch roots only (never the real repo), no running container touched (asc-chat-server-1 on 8347, asc-invoicing-web-1 on 8348), and no protected top-level file edited. Complexity low.

NOTE ON DEPLOYMENT, unrelated to the fix but discovered with it: AS-34's fix is merged to master but the running asc-chat-server-1 container has not been restarted, so the live service on 8347 is still executing pre-AS-34 code. Whoever picks this up should confirm whether a restart is wanted as part of it or as a separate deliberate act — restarting is a running-service action, not a code change.
title: chat /api/file: hard links bypass the AS-34 symlink policy; README over-claims by one mechanism
